title: Paul McCartney invites Hugh McCracken and Denny Seiwell to form a band | 1971
content:
Paul McCartney had played with guitarist Hugh McCracken and drummer Denny Seiwell extensively on the Ram album. Keen to form a new band, he invited the two Americans to visit the McCartneys’ Scottish farm in June 1971.

Denny and Monique Seiwell arrived at Glasgow Prestwick Airport on 22 June, bringing with them a drum kit at McCartney’s request. Pan Am arranged for a van driver to take them to Campbeltown, where they checked into the Argyll Arms and rented a car.

The following day they arrived at High Park Farm, the McCartneys’ Scottish hideaway. Denny set up his drums in the newly-named Rude Studio, and enjoyed the unspoilt scenery.

Hugh and Holly McCracken arrived in Scotland on 24 June. After a day of socialising with the others, he and Denny were told by Linda: “Come back tomorrow, but leave your wives at home this time, we’re going to make some music.”

On 25 June they jammed in Rude Studio. The songs included ‘Rode All Night’ and ‘Bip Bop’.

Later that day Paul asked if they would consider forming a band with him. Seiwell agreed, but McCracken was unsure. While both session musicians were in consistent demand in New York, the guitarist had young children from a previous marriage, and realised that moving to the UK would prevent him from seeing them grow up. After some days’ rumination, on 4 July he declined McCartney’s offer.

The offer remained open to Seiwell, but without a guitarist the band plan was put on hold. Seiwell returned to New York on 6 July, and McCartney rethought his plans.
